question.problem:
Compute the gradient of the function $f:{R}^{3}\to R$ defined by 

$$
f(x)={x}^{T}[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]x
$$

 with respect to $x$ at $x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$
question.worked_solution:
Writing $A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]$, we have

$$
f(x)={x}^{T}Ax.
$$

For a symmetric matrix $A$, the gradient of the function $f(x)={x}^{T}Ax$ with respect to $x\in {R}^{n}$ is

$$
{∇}_{x}f(x)=2Ax.
$$

Therefore, since $A$ is symmetric, we get

$$
{∇}_{x}f(x)=2[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$
